findings.comment: Plan documentation required: (1) identification of existing conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) on overhead lines; (2) dimension annotations showing minimum 15-foot radial clearance from buildings and other customer facilities to the outside conductor of distribution primary and neutral conductors; (3) clarification of whether existing lines are distribution or transmission voltage.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 in relation to distribution primary and neutral conductors on western and southern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 4, 9, and 21 confirm existing overhead electric (O.H.U.L.) facilities adjacent to the property. However, the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) are not labeled or identified on any plans. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies specifically to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. No dimension annotations show radial clearances from any building or customer facility to these conductors. No plan notes identify whether the existing lines are distribution (voltage <60kV) or transmission (voltage ≥60kV), and no conductor types are labeled.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (including buildings) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR of distribution primary and neutral conductors. Without identification of conductor types and without dimension annotations showing radial clearances from buildings to the conductors, compliance cannot be verified. The 15-foot clearance measurement requires identification of which conductors are primary/neutral vs. secondary, and this distinction is absent from the plans.

findings.comment: No registered surveyor proximity survey provided showing distances from proposed parking areas and site features to outside conductor of OHE line. Provide proximity survey documenting radial clearances from all customer facilities.
applicableAreas: Parking areas and site features on southern portion near OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 4 shows existing OHE line with associated utility poles. Sheet 9 shows the same OHE line routing along the southern boundary with parking areas, driveways, and site improvements in close proximity. The plans do not specify whether the overhead line serves distribution or transmission function, nor are the conductor types (primary, neutral, secondary) identified. No dimension annotations are provided showing distances from site facilities (parking, driveways, retaining walls) to the outside conductor. A registered surveyor proximity survey documenting existing and proposed facility locations relative to the OHE line is not provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires customer facilities (parking, driveways, site improvements) to maintain 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The distinction between distribution and transmission affects the applicable clearance standard. Without a registered surveyor proximity survey showing the conductor type, voltage level, and radial distances from all proposed facilities, compliance cannot be verified. The applicant has not submitted this required documentation.

findings.comment: Building elevation or section exhibits are required showing all projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, canopies) with dimension lines from the surveyed outside conductor location to the outermost edges of projections, demonstrating both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances.
applicableAreas: Building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, roofs) for Buildings 1-8
findings.observation: Site Plan (Sheet 9) shows buildings 1-8 with footprints and general layout, but no section views or elevation drawings depicting building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, patios) relative to overhead electric conductors. No surveyed conductor elevations are provided. Building architectural details or elevations showing projection dimensions are not included in the 39-sheet set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires building projections to maintain both (1) 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductors. Without section views or elevation drawings showing the vertical and horizontal relationships between building projections and the overhead conductors, and without surveyed conductor elevation data, compliance with these requirements cannot be verified. Buildings can only be shown in plan view without cross-sections showing their height relative to conductor height.

findings.comment: No building elevation or profile sheets provided showing vertical clearances from Building 8 roof and overhangs to overhead electric line. Provide engineered building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation and clearance dimension annotations.
applicableAreas: Building 8 roof and overhang areas adjacent to southern OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 9 shows Building 8 positioned adjacent to the southern boundary where the OHE line is routed. However, no building elevation or section views are provided on the site plan set that show the roof elevation of Building 8, any rooftop projections (overhangs, canopies, HVAC penetrations, vents), or their vertical clearance from the overhead line. No profile sections are provided showing the relationship between building projections and the conductor location. Building height is specified as 36'-1" but the finished floor and roof elevations are not dimensioned relative to the OHE line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance (horizontal) and implies vertical clearance verification for any building projections. Without profile or elevation sheets showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the building roof/overhang elevation dimensioned relative to that conductor, compliance cannot be determined. The applicant must provide elevation views with clearance dimensions for all building projections near the overhead line.

findings.comment: Surveyed elevations of overhead conductors with clearance dimension annotations from the outside conductor to building faces are required, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from electric facilities in the adjacent Valley View Road right-of-way.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1, 2, 8 adjacent to Valley View Road right-of-way where overhead electric facilities are located
findings.observation: Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions Survey) shows overhead utility lines and utility poles along Valley View Road (western boundary). Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows buildings 1, 2, and 8 positioned near the western property line adjacent to Valley View Road ROW. Building 1 is dimensioned at 26.1' from the western property line; Building 8 at 26.6'. However, NO surveyed conductor elevation data is shown, NO dimension annotations show clearances from buildings to the outside conductor, and NO section views demonstrate that permanent 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances are maintained from electric facilities in the adjacent ROW.
findings.reasoning: No surveyed elevation data or clearance dimensions provided showing that buildings adjacent to Valley View Road maintain required permanent clearances from outside conductor of overhead electric facilities in ROW. Proximity survey data by registered surveyor is needed.

findings.comment: Provide section views of retaining walls showing the surveyed overhead conductor elevation and clearance dimensions (measured horizontally) from the outside conductor location to the near face of the retaining wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls, particularly along southern property boundary where OHE line is located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows retaining walls labeled 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall' along the southern boundary and other site perimeter locations. Sheet 4 (Existing Conditions) shows an overhead electric line (O.H.U.L.) running along the southern property boundary. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans) provide wall construction sections showing max 14-foot height, reinforcement details, and structural dimensions, but contain NO sections showing clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor to the wall face or top. Wall plan sheets show only structural reinforcement and soil pressure calculations, not clearances to adjacent overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: The requirement under UCM § 1.10.3 is to maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outside conductor of overhead electric lines. Retaining walls up to 14 feet tall are proposed along the southern boundary where overhead electric lines are present. Without section views showing the surveyed conductor elevation and the distance (measured horizontally at ground level) from the conductor to the wall face, compliance cannot be verified. The wall height is known (up to 14 feet from foundation), but the conductor height and horizontal distance from the conductor to the wall are not documented.

findings.comment: Provide section view exhibits of each retaining wall showing the surveyed outside conductor location with dimension lines to the outermost edge (top/face) of the wall, demonstrating minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the conductor to the wall.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls adjacent to overhead electric facilities on southern and eastern boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plans and Wall Details) contain section views of retaining walls showing structural reinforcement, backfill requirements, footing details, and maximum heights (14 feet). However, these section views show only internal wall construction and soil pressure relationships. NO section views include dimension lines showing clearance from an outer electric conductor to the outermost edge (top or face) of the retaining wall. Sheet 9 shows OHE line along southern boundary, but Sheets 38-39 do not cross-reference or show the conductor on their wall sections.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 specifically requires 'Retaining walls lack section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of wall for clearance verification' to be addressed. This is an explicit documentation requirement. The wall construction sections present on Sheets 38-39 do not show the overhead conductor location or clearance dimensions from the conductor to the wall. The requirement is for section exhibits that include both the wall profile AND the conductor location with a dimensioned clearance.

findings.comment: Provide section views of parking areas with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimension annotations verifying minimum vertical clearance (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, or 18 feet for areas with truck traffic) from lowest point of conductors to finished parking surface. Add note to site plan specifying clearance requirement and designation of parking areas (truck vs. non-truck traffic).
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas beneath overhead electric lines
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows 10 surface parking spaces and 78 garage parking spaces for a total of 88 spaces (per site plan data table). The parking layout is shown on the plan view, but NO section views show vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric lines to the parking surface. Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows parking pad elevations and site topography but does not provide surveyed conductor heights or clearance verification. No note on site plan indicates the vertical clearance requirement or that parking must maintain minimum clearance from overhead lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.6.2 requires parking areas to maintain minimum vertical clearance from overhead electric lines (12 feet for residential pedestrian areas, 16 feet for parking without trucks, 18 feet with truck traffic). Without surveyed conductor elevations and section views showing the vertical relationship between parking pads and conductors, compliance cannot be verified. Additionally, a site plan note is required indicating the clearance requirement. No such note is present on Sheets 9 or 11.

findings.comment: Provide detailed photometric plan or lighting layout showing all proposed exterior and decorative light fixture locations with: (1) horizontal and vertical clearance dimensions from surveyed outside conductor locations; (2) confirmation that fixtures maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances, OR; (3) relocation notes if fixtures cannot meet clearance requirements. Include note on site plan indicating clearance requirement for lighting.
applicableAreas: Proposed exterior lighting fixtures throughout the site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan, Block 2) includes a 'Lighting Note' requiring all exterior lighting to be 'full cut-off and fully shielded in compliance with Subchapter E 2.5' and providing 'Figure 34: Examples of Fully-Shielded Light Fixtures.' This addresses design standards for light shielding but does NOT address clearances from overhead electric lines. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the site layout with various landscape elements but does not include dimension annotations showing horizontal or vertical clearances from proposed light fixtures to overhead electric lines. No site plan contains a photometric plan or detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations with clearance dimensions.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires decorative lighting proposed under existing overhead electric lines to meet clearance requirements (7.5-foot sky-to-ground horizontal, 15-foot radial) or be relocated. The site plan shows a general requirement for 'full cut-off' lighting compliance but does not identify where exterior lighting fixtures will be located or provide clearance verification from overhead conductors. Without a detailed lighting plan showing fixture locations and without clearance dimensions from conductors, compliance cannot be verified. If lighting is proposed beneath or within 15 feet of overhead conductors, relocation or clearance documentation is required.

findings.comment: Retaining walls are shown on the site plan around the perimeter (north, east, and south edges) and underground electric lines are routed near these locations, but no clearance dimensions or verification are documented showing that the required 5-foot minimum separation from duct banks is maintained. Provide clearance dimensions or notes on the electrical plan confirming that all retaining wall structures are positioned at least 5 feet from underground electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls shown along site perimeter (north, east, south boundaries)
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identifies multiple retaining wall segments throughout the site: a concrete retaining wall in the northeast corner along the biofiltration/detention pond, an existing retaining wall to be replaced along the entire eastern edge behind Buildings 5 and 6, and concrete retaining walls along the southern perimeter behind Buildings 7 and 8. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines forming a perimeter loop around the buildings, with the main lines running along the outer edges of the site where the retaining walls are located. However, no clearance dimensions are documented between the underground electric line routing and any of the retaining wall locations. No notes indicate that the required 5-foot separation has been verified. Sheet 38 (Wall Plan) would contain detailed wall dimensions and sections but was not reviewed in detail for this analysis.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires that permanent structures (including retaining walls) maintain minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric duct banks. The site plan shows both retaining walls and electric line routing in proximity to each other, but provides no documentation that this clearance requirement has been addressed. The absence of clearance dimensions or verification notes is a deficiency—required information is missing from the plans. While the general contractor verification notes reference utility coordination, they do not substitute for plan-based documentation showing that the clearance requirement has been satisfied.

findings.comment: Building elevations not provided showing relationship between proposed structures and overhead electric conductors. Provide building elevation sheets showing electric poles, cross arms (approximately 8 feet wide), and overhead conductors with dimensions confirming minimum 7.5-foot horizontal and 15-foot radial clearances per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities along western property boundary
Overhead electric facilities along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric facilities (OHE) marked with dashed lines along the western and southern property boundaries. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) also confirms the OHE line running along the southern boundary. Sheets 9 and 31 show the building footprints and layouts throughout the site. However, NO BUILDING ELEVATION SHEETS are included in the site plan submittal to verify the three-dimensional clearance between the proposed buildings and the overhead conductors. The vision analysis of Sheet 21 confirmed that overhead electric facilities are shown along boundaries but no elevation views or clearance exhibits are provided. The buildings shown on the site plan and landscape plan would need elevation drawings to verify they maintain the required 7.5-foot horizontal clearance and 15-foot radial clearance from overhead primary and neutral conductors per UCM § 1.10.3.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 establishes permanent clearance requirements from AE overhead distribution lines (7.5 feet horizontal, 15-foot radius). To verify compliance with these clearance requirements, building elevations must be provided showing the position of overhead conductors, poles, and cross arms relative to the proposed structures. The site plan shows the overhead facilities and building locations in plan view, but without elevation views and clearance exhibits, the three-dimensional clearance relationships cannot be determined. The 'Preliminary' designation of the electrical design may indicate coordination with Austin Energy is ongoing, but the site plan should include the necessary views to verify this critical clearance requirement. Without building elevation sheets showing these facilities, the deficiency status cannot be changed from 'unclear' to 'pass'.

findings.comment: Retaining wall heights and footing details near electric easements not clearly documented on grading plan. Provide wall top and bottom elevations on grading plan for walls located near overhead electric easements, with detailed cross-sections showing toe and heel footing configuration to verify clearance compliance per UCM § 1.10.3.
applicableAreas: Retaining walls along property boundaries near electric easements
findings.observation: Sheet 11 (Grading Plan) shows retaining walls labeled along property boundaries: 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall', 'Tie into existing Retaining Wall Match existing Wall Elevations', 'Existing Retaining Wall', and 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced'. The grading plan also shows electric easements ('5' Electric Easement', '15' Electric Easement') in the same boundary areas where retaining walls are located. However, the retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) are not clearly labeled on the grading plan in the areas near the electric easements. Sheets 38-39 (Wall Plan Details and Notes) would contain the detailed wall cross-sections and footing details. These details must be reviewed to determine if wall elevations and footing details near overhead electric facilities are adequately documented.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires that retaining wall heights and footing details be shown on grading plans when walls are proposed near overhead electric facilities to verify that the wall construction does not create clearance violations. The grouping specifies that 'Retaining wall heights (top and bottom elevations) not shown on grading plans or toe and heel footing details not provided for retaining walls near overhead electric facilities' is a deficiency. While walls are shown on Sheet 11 near electric easements, the specific top and bottom elevations are not clearly called out in those boundary areas. Whether detailed wall sections on Sheets 38-39 adequately document these clearances requires visual examination. The unclear status reflects uncertainty about whether the detail sheets (38-39) contain the required information.
